# Physical Consistency of Synthetic Data Generated by World Models: A 2D Navier-Stokes Study

This repository contains the computational code for the paper "Physical Consistency of Synthetic Data Generated by World Models: A 2D Navier-Stokes Study".

## Overview

We study the physical consistency of synthetic data generated by a VAE-LSTM world model trained on 2D Navier-Stokes fluid dynamics. We define six physical consistency metrics and compare synthetic data against RK4 direct numerical simulation and a persistence baseline.

## Files

- `experiment_v5.py` — Main experiment: 2D NS solver, VAE-LSTM world model, metric computation, statistical tests
- `spectral_analysis.py` — Spectral filter analysis: transfer function measurement, falsifiable prediction, phase-invariance test
- `generate_figures.py` — Figure generation (4 figures)
- `requirements.txt` — Python environment specification

## Usage

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python experiment_v5.py          # Run main experiment (trains model, computes metrics)
python spectral_analysis.py      # Run spectral filter analysis
python generate_figures.py       # Generate figures
```

## Key Results

- Synthetic data exhibits 144× smaller kinetic energy drift than fine-step RK4
- The world model acts as a spectral filter: T²(k) = f + A·exp(-(k/k_c)²), R² = 0.996
- Self-referential metrics (conservation) are improved by smoothing; reference-referential metrics (trajectory accuracy) are not
- Proposition: D_EN is invariant under phase randomization (Parseval's theorem)
